VU Computer Science combines programming and software engineering with algorithms, formal reasoning, mathematics, computer systems, networks, data and AI. Its general bachelor includes constrained second-year options, an open academic semester and a supervised scientific CS project.

UCR offers two qualified responses: computer systems, software and algorithms; and mathematical computing and intelligent systems. Both contain substantial actual computing and mathematical methods. The first retains more software-development and advanced-algorithm study; the second adds linear systems, calculus and robotic motion planning. These programmes have important gaps in dedicated hardware, web/security engineering, formal computation and the VU project sequence. Complementary design, cognition and communication courses do not remove those gaps.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: General Computer Science; three selected constrained choices

The general 2026–2027 route contains 60 EC compulsory study in Year 1; 45 EC compulsory study plus 15 EC constrained choices in Year 2; and 30 EC prescribed study plus 30 EC open academic study in Year 3. Academic Writing (3 EC), Computer Security (6 EC) and HCI (6 EC) are selected choices, not compulsory for everyone. There is no formal specialization. Object-Oriented and Functional Programming and Operating Systems require prior Computer Programming or Systems Programming Project; an approved earlier programming pair is also accepted for the former. Project entry requires at least 120 EC of the Computer Science bachelor. Students arrange a topic and supervisor before starting, normally in periods 5–6; a semester 1 project is possible through the coordinator. Internships require prior approval of a VU staff examiner. Projects may be individual or group work, with distinct student roles and individual assessment by two examiners: technical contribution 50%, thesis 40%, oral presentation 10%, each at least 5.5. The supervisor must submit the graded thesis and form by 31 July for August graduation or 31 January for February graduation. Generative AI is allowed for orientation and brainstorming, but cannot supply final-submission content. English diagnostic testing and the required refresher are mandatory without extra EC. BSA ordinarily requires 42 EC of first-year credits, subject to exceptions. Practical and tutorial attendance follows unit manuals; Smart Systems Engineering requires practical attendance and passing labs, with no practical resit. Thesis and placement regulations apply. Individual open choices need prior board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100. Abroad, at most one 6 EC master unit may be included and cannot be reused later. Eligible university or listed minors can be taken without prior board approval. The general Data Science and Basics of AI university minors are excluded for CS students; the CS-specific Business Analytics and Data Science minor remains eligible. Optional minors are not stacked.

A curriculum-level comparison of Computer Science at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with 2 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Computer systems, software and algorithms

Builds a substantial computing programme around Python programming, networks and operating systems, relational databases, C++ and functional software development, algorithms, discrete mathematics, statistics and AI methods. Product-design work contributes customer-needs analysis and prototyping, while philosophy, rhetoric and ethics develop critical argument and responsible practice. Those complementary subjects do not replace dedicated hardware, security, web engineering or the VU independent research project.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Mathematical computing and intelligent systems

Prioritizes mathematical computing and autonomous systems: linear algebra, numerical computation, linear-system transforms, calculus, statistics, machine learning, optimisation, vision and robotic motion planning. Programming, networks and databases remain substantial foundations. Introductory brain and behaviour supplies human cognition and research-method context for responsible AI; it does not implement human–computer interaction design. This direction trades software-development and advanced-algorithm depth for mathematical models and robotics.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

VU requires computer organization, web technology, smart systems engineering, systems programming, automata and complexity, and a supervised 15 EC CS project. The selected VU options add HCI and security. UCR has substantial programming, algorithms, systems, mathematics and AI, but leaves important specialist gaps. Product design and human cognition are complementary foundations, not replacements for these components.

The VU project requires a scientific question, literature, systematic investigation, a thesis and oral presentation. Individual or group projects are assessed individually by two examiners. UCR course projects do not automatically supply that independent research requirement; optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval.
